step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram represents the Omni channel B2B SaaS platform from Arvind Internet. 1. External traffic passes through AWS WAF for DDoS and bot protection, forwarding clean web traffic to an Application Load Balancer (ALB) which routes to Kubernetes (EKS) hosting 70+ microservices. 2. API Gateway handles internal and external API management and throttling, interacting with microservices (EKS) and the ElastiCache layer. 3. Code repositories and Jenkins (CI/CD) push container images to Elastic Container Registry (ECR), which are then deployed onto EKS. 4. Asynchronous communication between microservices is managed via message queues (SQS), pushing/pulling tasks and forwarding data to RDS MySQL. 5. Cached data in ElastiCache is processed/enriched and stored into persistent data stores like RDS MySQL.

graph.name: Arvind Internet Omni Platform Architecture
graph.notes: Architecture supports 35+ global brands, 6,000+ offline stores, and 3-5 million active sessions during peak season using 70+ microservices on Kubernetes.

nodes.name: WAF
nodes.notes: Mitigates malicious traffic, bot, and DDoS attacks for incoming web requests.

nodes.name: ALB
nodes.notes: Distributes incoming external web traffic to backend microservices.

nodes.name: API GW
nodes.notes: Handles throttling and routing for internal and external APIs across microservices.

nodes.name: K8S
nodes.notes: Hosts 70+ microservices running on Kubernetes containers for high-availability retail commerce.

nodes.name: CACHE
nodes.notes: In-memory caching layer used for processing and enriching non-transactional data.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Stores multi-terabyte transactional commerce and inventory data using MySQL.

nodes.name: QUEUE
nodes.notes: Handles asynchronous push/pull message queueing between microservices and storage.

nodes.name: ECR
nodes.notes: Elastic Container Registry storing container images for production deployment.

nodes.name: CI/CD
nodes.notes: CI/CD toolchain using Bitbucket, Fabricator, and Jenkins to build and package software.

edges.notes: WAF filters external traffic and sends clean traffic to ALB.
ALB forwards load-balanced traffic to Kubernetes microservices.
API Gateway routes throttled API requests to Kubernetes microservices.
API Gateway routes API caching requests to ElastiCache.
Jenkins builds and pushes docker images to ECR.
Images from ECR are pulled and deployed onto Kubernetes containers.
Microservices push asynchronous messages to SQS queue.
Microservices pull asynchronous task messages from SQS queue.
Asynchronous queued data is written into RDS database.
Enriched cached data is persisted to RDS database.
